content.text: I want to focus on DSL simplification. Every view should have 2 methods for defining modifiers and value. On top of that can container view have a method for content. The methods should be called with (values), modifiers (modifiers) and children (sub views). modifiers() and children() can be a variable number of modifiers or views. For values I am wondering if it should be a lambda with a config builder pattern and that the configuration defined there can be related (the same) as the one given to custom styles for views (fx. buttonstyle)
I'll research the current Java DSL to understand what we're simplifying.

1: package com.pathland.view;

3: import com.pathland.view.emit.PathlandNode;
4: 
5: /**
6:  * An interactive button ({@code Button}). Accepts an arbitrary child view as
7:  * the label. The control owns the native {@code BUTTON} node and wires the action on
8:  * it (whole button tappable, including its padding); the active {@link ButtonStyle}
9:  * (spec DSL.md §5.7) supplies the button's content — the label, decorated — as the
10:  * button node's child, so a composite label keeps its own layout.
11:  */
12: public final class Button implements View {
13: 
14:     private final View label;
15:     private final Runnable action;
16: 
17:     private Button(String title, Runnable action) {
18:         this(Text.of(title), action);
19:     }
20: 
21:     private Button(View label, Runnable action) {
22:         this.label = label;
23:         this.action = action;
24:     }
25: 
26:     /** A button with a plain text title. */
27:     public static Button of(String title, Runnable action) {
28:         return new Button(title, action);
29:     }
30: 
31:     /** A button with an arbitrary child view as its label. */
32:     public static Button of(View label, Runnable action) {
33:         return new Button(label, action);
34:     }
35: 
36:     @Override
37:     public PathlandNode render(Environment env) {
38:         // The control owns the native BUTTON shell + the action; the style supplies
39:         // the content (the decorated label) as the shell's child. The label keeps its
40:         // own component(s) and layout (Composite Override Mode, PRIMITIVES.md §2).
41:         PathlandNode node = new PathlandNode(Components.BUTTON);

9: /**
10:  * A view wrapped by one or more property modifiers (innermost-first) or a custom
11:  * {@link ViewModifier}. Property modifiers apply to the innermost built node and are
12:  * overwritten by outer modifiers ("outermost wins"); reactive modifiers record
13:  * a node-level binding so a signal change re-emits only that property.
14:  */
15: final class Modified implements View {
16: 
17:     /** One property application: a static value or a reactive signal. */
18:     record Prop(int property, Object value, Signal<?> signal) {
19: 
20:         static Prop value(int property, Object value) {
21:             return new Prop(property, value, null);
22:         }
23: 
24:         static Prop reactive(int property, Signal<?> signal) {
25:             return new Prop(property, null, signal);
26:         }
27:     }
28: 
29:     private final View inner;
30:     private final List<Prop> props;
31:     private final ViewModifier modifier;
32: 
33:     private Modified(View inner, List<Prop> props, ViewModifier modifier) {
34:         this.inner = inner;
35:         this.props = props;
36:         this.modifier = modifier;
37:     }
38: 
39:     /** A static property mod. */
40:     static Prop prop(int property, Object value) {
41:         return Prop.value(property, value);
42:     }
43: 
44:     /** A reactive property mod. */
45:     static Prop prop(int property, Signal<?> signal) {
46:         return Prop.reactive(property, signal);
47:     }
48: 
49:     /** Build a property-modifier view from inner + props. */
50:     static Modified props(View inner, Prop... props) {
51:         return new Modified(inner, List.of(props), null);
52:     }
53: 
54:     /** A custom-view-modifier wrapper. */
55:     static Modified apply(View inner, ViewModifier modifier) {
56:         return new Modified(inner, List.of(), modifier);
57:     }
58: 
59:     @Override
60:     public PathlandNode render(Environment env) {
61:         if (modifier != null) {
62:             return modifier.body(inner).render(env);
63:         }
64:         PathlandNode node = inner.render(env);
65:         for (Prop p : props) {
66:             if (p.signal() != null) {
67:                 Object value = ReactiveValues.from(p.property(), p.signal());
68:                 node.properties.put(p.property(), value);
69:                 node.propertyBindings.put(p.property(), p.signal());
70:             } else {
71:                 node.properties.put(p.property(), p.value());
72:             }
73:         }
74:         return node;
75:     }
76: }

1: # Pathland DSL Authoring Contract
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** October 1, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document defines the **authoring surface** — the SwiftUI-shaped DSL an
12: application developer writes — for every Pathland implementation. Where
13: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md), [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md), and
14: [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) describe the **wire surface** (component types,
15: property ids, events, opcodes), this file describes the **surface in source
16: code**: how views, controls, modifiers, and state are *named*, *ordered*, and
17: *composed* so that any language can expose a conformant, idiomatic DSL.
18: 
19: A DSL in a new language is **conformant** when it:
20: 
21: 1. exposes the full surface catalogued here (views, controls, modifiers,
22:    signals, state);
23: 2. maps every DSL element to the exact protocol component/property/event
24:    documented in the companion specs (no re-interpretation, no reallocation);
25: 3. produces **byte-identical opcode output** for the same source tree as the
26:    reference implementations (see the [Generation
27:    contract](#9-generation-contract-for-a-new-language)).
28: 
29: ### Relationship to the other specs
30: 
31: | File | Role |
32: |------|------|
33: | [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format: categories, commands, 16-byte opcode layout, ring/arena, value types |
34: | [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) | Which **views/nodes** exist and their component ids |
35: | [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md) | Which **modifiers** (properties) exist and how they encode |
36: | [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) | Which **core events** (raw inputs) exist and how they encode |
37: | [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) | Golden byte vectors |
38: | [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md) | Design-token catalog, resolution, and color-scheme contract |
39: | **DSL.md** (this file) | How an application **author** composes those into source code |
40: 
41: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
42: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. The Java DSL
43: > (`com.pathland.view`) and the Rust DSL (`pathland-view`) are the two reference
44: > realizations and are cited here by their **current signatures**; where they
45: > diverge from the canonical form below, that divergence is noted as a *delta*,
46: > and [§8](#8-java-dsl-convergence-adopted) records the adopted Java convergence.
47: > This document defines the contract only.
48: 
49: ### Two guiding rules
50: 
51: 1. **Stay as close to SwiftUI as possible.** View names, modifier names, and
52:    signature shapes mirror SwiftUI. Adapt only where the host language forces
53:    it (Rust snake_case + macros; Java camelCase + static factories), and never
54:    in a way that reorders or renames the canonical parameters.
55: 2. **State variables are signals.** Pathland does **not** use SwiftUI's
56:    `@State`/`@Binding` property wrappers. The view syntax is SwiftUI; the
57:    reactivity model is Angular-style signals (writable signals, computeds,
58:    effects, two-way bindings). A generated DSL MUST expose the signal surface
59:    of [§3](#3-state-model-signals).
60:

63: ## 1. Design principles (DSL-flavored)
64: 
65: These recap the protocol's non-negotiables in author-facing terms. A conformant
66: DSL must be *shaped* by them:
67: 
68: - **Declarative structure, never positions.** The DSL expresses `WHAT` — a
69:   `VStack`, a `HStack`, a `Text` — and constraint properties (spacing, padding,
70:   alignment, size hints). It never computes bounds and never emits rects.
71: - **`body()` is evaluated once at mount.** A composite view declares its
72:   subtree once; reactivity comes from **signals**, never from re-evaluating the
73:   body. This is what lets the emitter produce fine-grained
74:   `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` deltas instead of rebuilding the tree.
75:   The one sanctioned exception is a **structural container**
76:   ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering)): its content is
77:   re-evaluated on a signal change and the emitter reconciles the retained
78:   subtree into `TREE` deltas.
79: - **Modifiers are decoupled from views — and never hard-bound to a view
80:   type.** Any modifier applies to any view (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a
81:   `VStack` alike), and any developer can **author a custom modifier in
82:   application code** (a `ViewModifier`) that applies to any existing view —
83:   library primitive, container, control, custom view, or an already-modified
84:   view (see [§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)). A modifier a
85:   given renderer cannot apply is **allowed and ignored** — the property is
86:   still emitted.
87: - **There is exactly one modifier mechanism.** Built-in core modifiers are
88:   **not** a separate syntax: they are `ViewModifier` values the library ships,
89:   and the sugar methods (`.padding(_:)`, `.foregroundStyle(_:)`) are
90:   conveniences that construct them via `.with(...)`. Core and
91:   application-authored modifiers share the same surface.
92: - **There is exactly one style mechanism.** A customizable control/view takes
93:   its **content** from a *style* value (`ButtonStyle`, `LabelStyle`,
94:   `AudioStyle`, `VideoStyle`, …) scoped through the environment; the control
95:   owns its native component + interaction and the style owns the content
96:   ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)). Closed-variant/token
97:   styles (`ToggleStyle`, `PickerStyle`, `TextStyle`) are the same surface.
98: - **Constructor properties vs modifiers.** Structural/layout parameters
99:   (`alignment`, `spacing`) are **constructor arguments**, never chainable.
100:   Everything decorative (padding, color, font, frame, border, …) is a
101:   **chainable modifier**. There is no standalone width/height — use the
102:   compound `frame` modifier.
103: - **`Color` is never a modifier.** `Color` has SwiftUI's dual identity: it is a
104:   **View** (a layout-greedy solid-color fill) and a **Data Type** (passed into
105:   style-taking modifiers: `.foregroundStyle`, `.background`, `.border`,
106:   `.tint`). There is **no** `.color()` modifier, and `.foregroundColor(_:)` is
107:   deprecated — foreground styling is always `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
108: - **Only changes are transmitted.** Emission is diff-based; an unchanged tree
109:   emits **zero** opcodes. The DSL describes values; the emitter diffs them.
110: - **Typed enums, never raw ints.** Every enumerated value is a typed constant
111:   (`Alignment.leading`, `FontWeight.bold`, `ToggleStyle.checkbox`), not a bare
112:   integer. The numeric code is the DSL's job to resolve (see the value-type and
113:   enum tables in MODIFIERS.md).
114:

117: ## 2. Canonical signature notation
118: 
119: The canonical signatures below are written SwiftUI-shaped and language
120: agnostic. Conventions used:
121: 
122: - `T("…")` / `View("…")` — a view/control constructor.
123: - `{ ... }` — the child subtree (a trailing closure in SwiftUI; a vararg,
124:   macro, builder, or lambda in other languages).
125: - `Signal<T>` — a read-only derived or writable signal; `WritableSignal<T>` —
126:   a two-way binding target. A control takes a `WritableSignal<T>` for its
127:   value (see [§3](#3-state-model-signals)).
128: - `()` — the action a `Button` fires.
129: - `.with(name)` — apply a **modifier value** to a view; chainable on any
130:   view. Every modifier — built-in or application-authored — is such a value
131:   ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)); the sugar names
132:   (`.padding`, `.foregroundStyle`, …) are shorthand that construct the
133:   built-in values.
134: - Modifiers chain as `.name(args)` on any view and are applied
135:   **innermost-first** (the last chained modifier's property wins).
136: 
137: Per-language adaptation rules:
138: 
139: | Language | Case | Composition mechanism | Example |
140: |----------|------|-----------------------|---------|
141: | SwiftUI | `camelCase` | trailing closures + result builder | `VStack { Text("x").padding() }` |
142: | Java (`com.pathland.view`) | `camelCase` | `.of()` factories + varargs + `.with(...)`/`.with(...)` | `VStack.of(Text.of("x").with(Padding.of(16)))` |
143: | Rust (`pathland-view`) | `snake_case` | macros + free functions + chainable trait methods | `vstack![text("x").padding(16.0)]` |

147: ## 3. State model (signals)
148: 
149: Pathland state is **Angular-style signals**. This is the non-negotiable
150: reactive core every DSL exposes.
151: 
152: ### 3.1 Signal surface
153: 
154: | Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view.signal`) | Semantics |
155: |-----------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
156: | `signal(initial)` | `Signals.signal(T)` | a writable signal |
157: | `signal(name, initial)` | `Signals.signal(String, T)` | named (names surface in dependency errors) |
158: | `signal(initial, equal)` | `Signals.signal(T, BiPredicate<T,T>)` | custom equality |
159: | `computed(fn)` | `Signals.computed(Supplier<T>)` | lazy, memoized derived signal |
160: | `effect(fn)` | `Signals.effect(Runnable)` | runs immediately, then on dependency change |
161: | `untracked(fn)` | `Signals.untracked(Supplier<T>)` | reads without recording dependencies |
162: | `read()` | `get()` | current value |
163: | `write(v)` | `set(T)` | replace (no-op when equal) |
164: | `update(fn)` | `update(UnaryOperator<T>)` | derive from current and write |
165: | `asReadonly()` | `asReadonly()` | read-only view of a writable signal |
166: 
167: **Guarantees** (must be preserved by any implementation): equality suppression,
168: synchronous flush at the end of the outermost write, glitch-free propagation
169: (each computed recomputes at most once per flush), error caching, write
170: discipline, and circular-dependency detection.
171: 
172: ### 3.2 Two-way binding
173: 
174: A control's value is **a `WritableSignal<T>` passed to its constructor**:
175: `TextField(placeholder, writable)`, `Toggle(label, isOn: writable)`,
176: `Slider(value: writable, in: min...max)`. The flow:
177: 
178: 1. At **mount**, the DSL control records a **value input** (a sink on the
179:    retained node) for the signal, and the emitter exposes routing registries to
180:    the host: tap actions, text inputs, value inputs, date inputs.
181: 2. The host receives the control's raw event (`TEXT_CHANGED`,
182:    `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED`, or a composed tap) and calls the sink,
183:    which **writes into the signal**.
184: 3. The signal flush re-emits **only that node's** delta (`SET_TEXT`,
185:    `SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_DATE`) back through the emitter.
186: 
187: Reading is equally fine-grained: a node's text or a property can be **bound to
188: a signal** (`Text(signal)`, `.foregroundStyle(signal)`, `.fontSize(signal)`),
189: so a change re-emits only the bound node.
190: 
191: ### 3.3 Persisted state (`State<T>`)
192: 
193: A `State<T>` field is the SwiftUI-`@State`-shaped form of a persisted signal,
194: **auto-wired by key**:
195: 
196: ```java
197: State<Integer> count = new State<>(0);            // key = field name "count"
198: State<Integer> total = new State<>(0, "total");   // explicit store key
199: count.get(); count.set(0); count.update(v -> v + 1);
200: count.signal();                                   // the WritableSignal (for TextField, …)
201: ```
202: 
203: The store (`StateStore`) is untyped and platform-neutral (in-memory, Redis,
204: file, SQLite, LocalStorage, NVS flash). The Java realization wires `State`
205: fields via an annotation processor that generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per
206: view class; connection happens when the view renders. A generated DSL in a
207: language without reflection/annotation processing MUST offer the equivalent
208: explicit wiring.
209: 
210: ### 3.4 Structural reactivity (conditional rendering)
211: 
212: The tree is normally static once mounted (["`body()` is evaluated once at
213: mount"](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)); the **only** sanctioned way to
214: change *structure* reactively is a **structural container**: a slot whose
215: single child subtree is selected by a signal and **reconciled** when the
216: signal changes. This is the foundation for `if`/`else`, `switch`, and
217: navigation ([§4.5](#45-navigation)).
218: 
219: | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Rust DSL (current) | Emits |
220: |----------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|-------|
221: | `if cond { then } else { else }` in a result builder | `Conditional.when(Signal<Boolean>, View then, View else)` | plain `if`/`match` in `build()` | `TREE` deltas (reconcile) |
222: | `switch value { case a -> v; default -> d }` | `Conditional.when(Signal<T>, Case.of(T, View)...)` + `Case.otherwise(View)` | plain `if`/`match` in `build()` | `TREE` deltas (reconcile) |
223: 
224: **Java realization** (`com.pathland.view.Conditional`): statically importable
225: lowercase factories on a final class with a private constructor, mirroring
226: [`Signals`](#31-signal-surface):
227: 
228: ```java
229: import static com.pathland.view.Conditional.when;
230: import static com.pathland.view.Conditional.Case;
231: 
232: when(showLogin, LoginView.of(), HomeView.of());              // if / else
233: when(mode,
234:     Case.of(RouteMode.HOME, HomeView.of()),
235:     Case.of(RouteMode.USERS, UsersView.of()),
236:     Case.otherwise(NotFoundView.of()));                      // switch + default
237: ```
238: 
239: The names `if`, `switch`, `case`, and `else` are Java reserved keywords, so
240: `when` (Kotlin's `switch` analog, and a valid Java identifier) is the method
241: name, and `Case.of(...)` / `Case.otherwise(...)` carry the branches. A boolean
242: signal takes the two-branch overload (`then`, `else`); an enum/int/string
243: signal takes keyed `Case` branches typed to the signal's value type, with an
244: optional `Case.otherwise` default.
245: 
246: **Emission contract** (the body-once exception, formalized):
247: 
248: 1. A structural container holds a **stable slot node** (a `Group`, see
249:    [§8](#8-java-dsl-convergence-adopted)) whose single child is the currently
250:    selected content. Selection is a **content function** over the selector
251:    signal — `if`/`else` and `switch` are sugar over it, so value-parametrized
252:    content (e.g. a route param) is a first-class case.
253: 2. On selector change the container re-evaluates the content function,
254:    **renders the new subtree**, and the emitter **reconciles** it against the
255:    retained snapshot — emitting only `TREE` deltas (`CREATE_NODE` /
256:    `DELETE_NODE` / `INSERT_CHILD` / `REMOVE_CHILD` / `MOVE_CHILD`).
257: 3. **Identical structure emits zero opcodes.** The reconcile diffs old vs new;
258:    a recompute that yields the same structure produces no `TREE` deltas, so no
259:    equality predicate is needed on the selector signal.
260: 4. Structural containers **nest**: a container inside a container re-evaluates
261:    and reconciles its own slot independently.
262: 5. All other reactivity stays fine-grained (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`); a
263:    structural container never re-emits siblings or ancestors.
264: 
265: **Rust delta**: the Rust DSL builds `Node` trees directly and the host rebuilds
266: + re-`assign_id`s + diffs on every interaction, so plain `if`/`match` in
267: `build()` already produces the same reconcile — no wrapper slot and no special
268: type. An optional `switch!` macro is sugar.

304: 
305: | View | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Emits / Binds |
306: |------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
307: | `VStack` | `VStack(alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `VStack.of(View...)` / `VStack.of(HorizontalAlignment, float, View...)` | `VSTACK` 0x10; `SPACING` 0x0001, `ALIGNMENT` 0x0002, `CONTENT_MARGINS` 0x0005 |
308: | `HStack` | `HStack(alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `HStack.of(View...)` / `HStack.of(VerticalAlignment, float, View...)` | `HSTACK` 0x11 |
309: | `ZStack` | `ZStack(alignment:) { … }` | `ZStack.of(View...)` / `ZStack.of(Alignment, View...)` | `ZSTACK` 0x12; `ALIGNMENT` |
310: | `Grid` | `Grid(columns:rows:alignment:spacing:) { … }` | `Grid.of(View...)` / `Grid.of(int columns, View...)` / `Grid.of(int columns, int rows, View...)` / `Grid.of(int columns, int rows, Alignment, float, View...)` / `Grid.of(List<GridItem>, View...)` / `Grid.of(List<GridItem>, Alignment, float, View...)` | `GRID` 0x13; `GRID_COLUMNS` 0x001E, `GRID_ROWS` 0x001F, `GRID_TRACKS` 0x0020 |

326: using varargs (`VStack.of(children...)`), not a builder/trailing-closure
327: block. Constructor layout properties come as a separate overload
328: (`VStack.of(Alignment, float, View...)`). The canonical SwiftUI form passes

331: **Grid counts**: `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` are **constructor properties**

335: count is `int` in the DSL and emits a positive F32; absent = auto-fit. The
336: static `Grid` takes optional `columns:`/`rows:` (both absent = SwiftUI `Grid`
337: auto-fit); `LazyVGrid` takes `columns:`; `LazyHGrid` takes `rows:`.
338: 
339: **`GridItem` (per-track sizes)**: a **`List<GridItem>`** overload expresses
340: per-track sizes (SwiftUI `GridItem` / Compose `GridCells` parity) —
341: `GridItem.flexible()` (`flex`), `GridItem.fixed(pts)` (`fixed:<pts>`),
342: `GridItem.adaptive(min)` (`adaptive:<min>`). The list serializes to the
343: `GRID_TRACKS` STRING property (comma-separated), which **takes precedence** over
344: the counts; a count overload is the `N`×`flexible` sugar. CSS-grid-native —
345: renderers without a native per-track equivalent size tracks naturally
346: (renderer status, spec/PRIMITIVES.md §grid model).

348: ### 4.3 Semantic controls
349: 
350: Two-way value controls bind a `WritableSignal`. Actions bind a callback.
351: 
352: | Control | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Emits / Binds |
353: |---------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
354: | `Button` | `Button("title", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `Button.of(String, Runnable)` / `Button.of(View, Runnable)` | `BUTTON` 0x20 (control node); the label is its **child** via the active `ButtonStyle` ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)); tap = composed `POINTER_DOWN`+`POINTER_UP` |
355: | `TextField` | `TextField("placeholder", text: writable)` | `TextField.of(String, WritableSignal<String>)` | `TEXT_FIELD` 0x21; `TEXT_CHANGED` → text input |
356: | `SecureField` | `SecureField("…", text: writable)` | (secure via `IS_SECURE` token) | `TEXT_FIELD` 0x21 + `IS_SECURE` 0x200D |
357: | `TextEditor` | `TextEditor(text: writable)` | `TextEditor.of(WritableSignal<String>)` | `TEXT_EDITOR` 0x22 |
358: | `Toggle` | `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `Toggle.of(boolean, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` / `Toggle.of(String label, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` / `Toggle.of(ToggleStyle, boolean, WritableSignal<Boolean>, String)` | `TOGGLE` 0x24; `VALUE_CHANGED` → value input; `TOGGLE_STYLE` 0x2018 |
359: | `Slider` | `Slider(value: writable, in: min...max)` | `Slider.of(WritableSignal<Float>, float min, float max)` | `SLIDER` 0x25; `VALUE_CHANGED` → value input |
360: | `Stepper` | `Stepper("label", value: writable, in: min...max, step:)` | `Stepper.of(WritableSignal<Float>, float min, float max, float step)` | `STEPPER` 0x26; `VALUE_CHANGED` → value input |
361: | `DatePicker` | `DatePicker("label", selection: writable, displayedComponents:)` | `DatePicker.of(DatePickerMode, WritableSignal<Integer>)` | `DATE_PICKER` 0x27; `DATE_CHANGED` → date input; value via `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` |
362: | `Picker` | `Picker("label", selection: writable) { options }` | `Picker.of(PickerStyle, WritableSignal<Integer>, View... options)` | `PICKER` 0x28; `VALUE_CHANGED` (index) → value input |
363: | `Menu` | `Menu { actions } label: { trigger }` | `Menu.of(View trigger, View... actions)` / `Menu.of(View, WritableSignal<Integer>, View...)` | `MENU` 0x29; `VALUE_CHANGED` (item index) → value input |
364: | `ColorPicker` | `ColorPicker("label", selection: writable)` | `ColorPicker.of(WritableSignal<Color>)` | `COLOR_PICKER` 0x2A; `VALUE_CHANGED` (packed `0xAARRGGBB` as f32) → value input |
365: 
366: **Deltas (Java)**: the value binding is **binding-first** in `.of(...)` —
367: `Slider.of(binding, min, max)` reads the initial value from the signal (the
368: single source of truth) instead of SwiftUI's labeled `value:in:` range
369: binding. `Button` takes a `(label, action)` pair rather than SwiftUI's
370: `Button("title") { action }` trailing-action form. `Toggle` offers the
371: SwiftUI-closer `of(label, isOn)`; `DatePicker` binds **days-since-epoch**
372: (`WritableSignal<Integer>`) rather than a date object — the protocol's
373: `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` two-field encoding is days + millis-of-day (see
374: [§8](#8-java-dsl-convergence-adopted)).
375: 
376: **Control guarantees** (from PRIMITIVES.md): a control without children renders
377: in **Native Token Mode** (native OS control); a control with a child subtree
378: renders in **Composite Override Mode** (custom chrome wrapped with native
379: gesture semantics). A **style** supplies that child subtree — the control owns
380: the native component + interaction, the style owns the content
381: ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)). Renderers MUST gate
382: value/text/date events by `BINDING_ID`, `ACTION_ID`, or the `EVENT_LISTENERS`
383: bitmask (transport-aware event guards) — see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md).

385: ### 4.4 Gestures
386: 
387: | Gesture | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Rust DSL (current) |
388: |---------|---------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
389: | tap | `.onTapGesture { action }` | `.with(TapGesture.of(Runnable))` | `.on_tap_gesture(f)` |
390: | raw pointer | `.gesture` composition from raw inputs | `.with(PointerEvents.of(int mask))` | `.pointer_events(u32 mask)` |
391: 
392: Tap is **not** a protocol event: it is composed app-side from `POINTER_DOWN`
393: then `POINTER_UP` on the same target (`EVENT_LISTENERS` bits 0|2). The
394: `TapGesture` modifier value declares those listeners and records the action;
395: the host routes the recognized tap via the emitter's tap-action registry.
396: 
397: ### 4.5 Navigation
398: 
399: Navigation is **structural reactivity over a route signal**
400: ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering)): a
401: `NavigationContainer` is a structural container whose content function is
402: route-table matching. The wire surface is minimal and entirely optional:
403: `ROUTE` (MODIFIERS.md `0x2019`, a STRING current-path property on the slot),
404: `NAV_DEPTH` (MODIFIERS.md `0x201A`, a U32 back-stack-depth property on the
405: slot), `NAV_CHROME` (MODIFIERS.md `0x201B`, an F32-enum chrome-mode property
406: on the slot), `TRANSITION` (MODIFIERS.md `0x1031`, a presentation hint), and
407: the `NAVIGATE` event (EVENTS.md `0x0E`, host→guest). Renderers stay
408: stateless: they render whatever destination subtree the app emits and **may**
409: animate a swap when the `TRANSITION` hint is present, but must render normally
410: when they ignore it.
411: 
412: **Navigation is opt-in — the developer declares it by inserting a
413: `NavigationContainer`.** A tree without one has no navigation and the renderer
414: adds none. The container's chrome mode decides who supplies the navigation UI:
415: 
416: - `PlatformDefault` (default): the **renderer** supplies the chrome — the
417:   platform's native navigation container where one exists, and a renderer-drawn
418:   back affordance where none exists. `NavigationContainer.of(router)`.
419: - `Custom`: the **developer owns all navigation UI** — they draw their own
420:   back buttons / bars in the destinations and call `router.back()` /
421:   `navigate(...)` directly; the renderer adds no chrome (no native header-bar
422:   back button, no DOM back button). `NavigationContainer.of(router, Chrome.CUSTOM)`.
423:   Renderers treat a missing `NAV_CHROME` as `PlatformDefault`.
424: 
425: | View | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Rust DSL (current) | Emits / Binds |
426: |------|----------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|---------------|
427: | `NavigationContainer` | `NavigationStack(path:) { destination(for:) }` | `NavigationContainer.of(Router)` / `.of(Router, Chrome.CUSTOM)` | `NavigationContainer::new(Router)` | a `Group` slot + `ROUTE` `0x2019`, `NAV_DEPTH` `0x201A`, `NAV_CHROME` `0x201B`, `TRANSITION` `0x1031`; destination swap = `TREE` deltas |
428: | `NavigationLink` | `NavigationLink("label", value:)` | `NavigationLink.of(String, Router, String to)` / `NavigationLink.of(String, String to)` (router-agnostic) | `navigation_link(...)` | a `BUTTON` whose tap pushes `to` (via the router, or resolved to the nearest enclosing router when router-agnostic) |
429: | `RouteTable` | — | `RouteTable` (builder), or `Navigation.navigator(...)` (the ergonomic facade) | `RouteTable::new(...)` | none (app-side matching) |
430: 
431: **Router state** — app-owned (never renderer state):
432: 
433: - `Route` = absolute path + path params (`/users/:id` → `{id:"42"}`) + query.
434:   Path params are strings; typed params are a DSL concern.
435: - `RouteTable` maps path patterns to destination factories, captures params,
436:   and runs **guards**; a guard redirects via `replace()`. Factories are lazy —
437:   in the SSR model the client only ever receives the chosen destination's
438:   deltas.
439: - `Router` owns a `Signal<Route>` plus a **back-stack** and exposes
440:   `navigate` / `push` / `pop` / `replace` / `back`. `push` appends; `pop` /
441:   `back` step back; `navigate` / `replace` set the current route. The current
442:   path is emitted as the `ROUTE` property on the container slot.
443: - The route is a **plain signal — not persisted**. On the web the URL is the
444:   persistence layer (the DOM client mirrors it via `pushState`/`popstate`); on
445:   native the route is per-session.
446: - The initial route is delivered as a **`META::ENVIRONMENT` `ROUTE` field**
447:   (host → guest platform environment, OPCODE.md — the same message that carries
448:   the viewport): on SSR the host synthesizes it from the HTTP request (the
449:   request path — all the request offers), and over the WebSocket the DOM client
450:   sends it (with the viewport) as its **first** message and later **enriches**
451:   the environment (a window-resize re-emits the viewport; future platform
452:   fields arrive the same way). The application applies the environment
453:   uniformly — the router hydrates from the `ROUTE` field before mount, so a
454:   deep-link request renders the right destination on the first frame. The app
455:   never models the platform's location handling — history adaptation
456:   (`pushState` / `replaceState` / back) is a renderer/DOM-client translation of
457:   the `ROUTE` property and the `NAVIGATE` event.
458: 
459: **Reserved framework root** — the host reserves **`/_pathland/**`** for its own
460: system endpoints, so app routes never collide with them: the WebSocket lives at
461: `/_pathland/ws`, the DOM-client bundle under a **content-hashed name**
462: (`/_pathland/dom-renderer-<sha256>.js`; the current name is published next to the
463: copies in the one-line pointer `/_pathland/dom-renderer.current`, read by the SSR
464: layer so the page always references the built artifact — the fresh URL per build
465: busts immutable asset caches), the
466: renderer-owned icon glyphs at `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` (served from the
467: shared HTML-renderer library — `pathland_html_icon_svg` over the C ABI — which
468: the DOM client lazily fetches when a delta references an `ICON_NAME` the page
469: did not embed), and the host's asset mount at `/_pathland/assets/**`. App routes
470: are everything else (served by the SSR catch-all). The DOM client reads the
471: base from the SSR page's `data-pathland-base` attribute (default `/_pathland`),
472: so a host can relocate it behind a proxy. Asset references in the UI model are
473: **absolute** (`/_pathland/assets/icons/home.svg`) so deep-linked routes resolve
474: correctly.
475: 
476: **The `Navigation` facade** — the ergonomic entry point. `Navigation.navigator`
477: collapses the route table + router + seeding into one readable flow, and
478: `Navigation.of(router)` is the container:
479: 
480: ```java
481: Router router = Navigation.navigator("/kitchen")     // seeds the initial path
482:     .route("/",          new HomeView())             // View overload (no params)
483:     .route("/users/:id", params -> new UserView(params.intValue("id")))
484:     .fallback(new NotFoundView())
485:     .build();
486: 
487: View shell = Navigation.of(router);                  // == NavigationContainer.of(router)
488: Signal<Boolean> onKitchen = Navigation.isActive(router, "/kitchen");
489: ```
490: 
491: - `.route(String, View)` for no-param destinations; `.route(String, RouteHandler)`
492:   for param destinations; guarded variants take a `Predicate<Params>` + a redirect
493:   target; `.fallback(View | RouteHandler)` is the 404. `build()` returns the
494:   seeded `Router` (the initial path flows through the same guard matching).
495: - **`Params`** replaces the raw `Map<String,String>` in `RouteHandler` with typed
496:   access: `params.get("id")`, `params.intValue("id")`, `params.longValue(...)`,
497:   `params.doubleValue(...)`, `params.booleanValue(...)`, `params.path()`.
498: - **`Navigation.isActive(router, path)` → `Signal<Boolean>`** is a reactive
499:   "is this the active route" signal derived from the router's route signal —
500:   style an active menu row or gate conditional content:
501:   `Signals.computed(() -> Navigation.isActive(router, path).get() ? ACTIVE : CLEAR)`.
502: - **The environment is the one scoping system** (SwiftUI `.environment`): values
503:   are bound down a subtree with `View.environment(key, value)` and read with
504:   `Environment.value(key)`; nearest wins. Styles use it too — `buttonStyle`
505:   binds `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE` (`EnvironmentKey<ButtonStyle>`), so a style
506:   scoped above a structural container survives its destination re-render.
507: - **The router as a scoped environment value** (SwiftUI `.environment` style):
508:   `Navigation.ROUTER` is an `EnvironmentKey<Router>`. A `NavigationContainer` scopes
509:   it to its destination subtree; any component reads
510:   `Environment.value(Navigation.ROUTER)` during render — no constructor threading,
511:   nearest binding wins (nested containers override), and structural slots re-apply
512:   the scope when they re-render their destination.
513: - **Environment reads always return a signal** (`Environment.value(key)` →
514:   `Signal<T>`): a value injected as a `Signal` comes back as the same instance, so a
515:   node bound to it (e.g. `Text.of(Environment.value(key))`) re-emits when it changes;
516:   a plain value is wrapped in a constant signal (`.get()` gives the value). Inject a
517:   reactive value with `view.environment(key, signal)`. A read made **before the key is
518:   bound** (e.g. in a field initializer, before the enclosing `.environment(...)` scope
519:   is pushed) returns a **lazy signal** that captures the binding on the first `.get()`
520:   during render — the SwiftUI `@Environment` field style:
521:   ```java
522:   private final Signal<Router> router = Environment.value(Navigation.ROUTER);
523:   @Override public View body() { ... menuRow(router.get(), ...) ... }
524:   ```
525: 
526: **The active platform path is universal** — `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` is an
527: `EnvironmentKey<String>` the host provides for **every** app (with
528: or without navigation), like SwiftUI's `onOpenURL` generalized across platforms:
529: ```java
530: // host (always):
531: WritableSignal<String> activePath = Signals.signal(env.route());
532: RenderResult result = emitter.mount(
533:         root.environment(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH, activePath), new Environment(state));
534: // re-route on deep-link/popstate:
535: activePath.set(env.route());   // or from a NAVIGATE event URL
536: ```
537: - **An app with navigation** builds a **router bound to the signal**:
538:   `Navigation.navigator().route(...).build(Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH))`.
539:   The signal is the source of truth: external writes (deep links/popstate) are
540:   re-routed **through guards** (never bypassed), and the router's own
541:   `navigate`/`push`/`pop`/`replace` are mirrored back into the signal when it is
542:   writable (the host's `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` always is). The initial value is
543:   guard-processed.
544: - **An app without navigation** just observes the signal — read it, or register
545:   `View.onPathChange(path -> …)` (fires on every change, including the initial value).
546: - `NAVIGATE` events: a URL updates `activePath` (→ bound router re-routes guard-aware,
547:   `onPathChange` listeners fire); a back (no URL) goes to `RenderResult.navigateHandler`
548:   → `router.pop()` — meaningful only when a router exists.
549: 
550: **Any component can change the route** — declarative navigation intents. A
551: component anywhere *inside* a `NavigationContainer` can change the route without
552: threading a `Router` by hand, using a `NavigationMod` on a `BUTTON`:
553: 
554: ```java
555: Button.of("Go to kitchen").navigate("/kitchen");  // direct selection
556: Button.of("Open item").push("/item/1");           // drill-down (back-stack)
557: Button.of("Swap").replace("/settings");           // guard redirect / replace
558: NavigationLink.of("Users", "/users");             // router-agnostic (pushes)
559: ```
560: 
561: - The intent (`navigateTo` + a `NavOp` — `NAVIGATE`/`PUSH`/`REPLACE`) is
562:   recorded on the node at render.
563: - The **emitter resolves it to the nearest enclosing `Router`** — the
564:   `NavigationContainer` whose subtree the component lives under — while walking
565:   the retained tree (nested containers resolve to the innermost one). No
566:   hidden global, no environment lookup.
567: - The resolved action is exposed on `RenderResult.navigateActions`
568:   (`node id → Runnable`), a live map like `tapActions`; the host routes a tap
569:   on that node to the action (checked before `tapActions`).
570: - A `NavigationContainer` whose subtree *is* a destination resolves its own
571:   router, so the sidebar's own menu rows (which sit *outside* the container, as
572:   the developer's custom chrome) capture the router explicitly — the
573:   nearest-enclosing mechanism covers components inside a container.
574: 
575: **URL sync (web)** — the app owns state; the browser mirrors it:
576: 
577: 1. On a route change the app emits the new path as `ROUTE`; the DOM client
578:    reacts with `history.pushState` (v1 always pushes; `replaceState` for
579:    `replace()` is a documented follow-up).
580: 2. Browser back/forward fire `popstate`; the DOM client sends a `NAVIGATE`
581:    event with the new URL over the event path; the host routes it into the
582:    router (`handlePlatformNavigation`), which matches and re-emits.
583: 3. No sync loop: a server-originated `pushState` never fires `popstate`. On
584:    initial SSR hydrate the URL is already correct — no `pushState`.
585: 
586: **Native back** — platform back affordances (Android predictive-back, iOS
587: swipe-back, a desktop back button) map to a `NAVIGATE` event **without** a URL
588: payload (= "back one step"); the host calls `router.pop()`. The renderer never
589: decides navigation — it only requests it.
590: 
591: **Native integration** — each renderer **may** promote a `NavigationContainer`
592: slot onto its platform navigation affordance. The trigger is structural, not a
593: new primitive: a slot carrying the `ROUTE` (STRING) property is a navigation
594: slot and may be rendered as the platform's native navigation container. The
595: contract keeps the renderer stateless:
596: 
597: - **App owns** the route signal, the back-stack, and which destination is
598:   current; it emits the current destination as the slot child plus `ROUTE`
599:   and `NAV_DEPTH`.
600: - **Renderer owns** the native chrome and presentation only: it maps the slot's
601:   child swaps onto native push/pop, uses `ROUTE` for native path parity and
602:   `NAV_DEPTH` to reconcile its page stack (push when deeper, replace the top
603:   when the depth is unchanged, pop down on a depth decrease), uses `TRANSITION`
604:   (0x1031) to choose a native transition (fade/slide/scale), and
605:   translates every native back affordance (a header-bar back button, a
606:   swipe/gesture, a platform back key, predictive back) into a `NAVIGATE` event
607:   **without** a URL payload (= "back one step"). The renderer never holds the
608:   back-stack and never decides navigation — it renders whatever destination
609:   subtree the app emits and may animate the swap.
610: - Platforms with no native navigation container render the slot as an ordinary
611:   container that swaps children in
612:   place; the app's own back-stack is the only stack. The app does not branch on
613:   platform — the same `NavigationContainer` works on both, and the renderer's
614:   use (or not) of a native container is purely a presentation decision.
615: 
616: **Deltas (Java)**: `Router` / `RouteTable` live in
617: `com.pathland.view.router`; `Conditional` in `com.pathland.view`. The
618: `NavigationContainer` is a structural container, so `if`/`switch`-style sugar
619: is the `Conditional.when` form of [§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering).

623: ## 5. Modifier surface
624: 
625: Properties, value types, and emission rules come from
626: [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md); the tables here give the **DSL signature**. A
627: compound SwiftUI modifier expands to **one `SET_PROPERTY` per underlying
628: property** (`.frame` → `WIDTH` + `HEIGHT` + `ALIGNMENT`; `.border` →
629: `BORDER_COLOR` + `BORDER_WIDTH`; `.shadow` → `SHADOW_COLOR` + `SHADOW_RADIUS` +
630: `SHADOW_X` + `SHADOW_Y`). `Java DSL (current)` is the reference realization.
631: 
632: **One mechanism for every modifier.** Each entry in the tables below is a
633: `ViewModifier` value. `padding(16)` is shorthand for
634: `.with(Padding.of(16))`; `foregroundStyle(color)` for
635: `.with(ForegroundStyle.of(color))`. The tables list the canonical sugar
636: names; core and application-authored modifiers use the same `.with(...)`
637: surface ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).
638: 
639: > **Java realization**: the Java DSL ships **no modifier sugar on `View`** —
640: > modifiers are values applied via `.with(X.of(...))` (single) or
641: > `.with(X.of(...), Y.of(...))` (several, innermost-first). The "Java DSL
642: > (current)" column lists the value form; the parameter list is carried from the
643: > canonical signature.
644: 
645: ### 5.1 Layout & frame
646: 
647: | Modifier | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Property(ies) |
648: |----------|---------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
649: | `frame` | `.frame(width:height:alignment:)` | `.with(FrameMod.of(float width))` / `.with(FrameMod.of(float width, float height))` / `.with(FrameMod.of(float width, float height, Alignment))` — the 2D `Alignment` positions the content within the box; omitted → no `ALIGNMENT` emitted, a stack's own alignment is preserved | `WIDTH` 0x100B, `HEIGHT` 0x100C, `ALIGNMENT` 0x0002 (only when provided) |
650: | `frame(min:…)` | `.frame(minWidth:idealWidth:maxWidth:minHeight:idealHeight:maxHeight:)` | `.with(FrameMod.of(float, float, float, float, float, float))` (NaN = unset) | `MIN_WIDTH` 0x0012 … `MAX_HEIGHT` 0x0017 |
651: | `padding` | `.padding(_:)` / `.padding(_:edges:)` | `.with(Padding.of(int))` / `.with(Padding.of(float))` / `.with(Padding.of(int top, int right, int bottom, int left))` | `PADDING` 0x1011 / `PADDING_TOP` 0x1012 … `PADDING_LEFT` 0x1015 |
652: | `offset` | `.offset(x:y:)` | `.with(Offset.of(float x, float y))` | `OFFSET_X` 0x000E, `OFFSET_Y` 0x000F |
653: | `position` | `.position(x:y:)` | `.with(Position.of(float x, float y))` | `POSITION_X` 0x0010, `POSITION_Y` 0x0011 |
654: | `fixedSize` | `.fixedSize()` / `.fixedSize(horizontal:vertical:)` | `.with(FixedSize.of())` / `.with(FixedSize.of(boolean, boolean))` | `FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL` 0x0018, `FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL` 0x0019 |
655: | `layoutPriority` | `.layoutPriority(_:)` | `.with(LayoutPriority.of(float))` | `LAYOUT_PRIORITY` 0x001A |
656: | `zIndex` | `.zIndex(_:)` | `.with(ZIndex.of(float))` | `Z_INDEX` 0x100F |
657: | `aspectRatio` | `.aspectRatio(_:contentMode:)` | `.with(AspectRatio.of(float, ContentMode))` | `ASPECT_RATIO` 0x001B, `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C |
658: | `scaledToFit` | `.scaledToFit()` | `.with(ScaledToFit.of())` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C (Fit) |
659: | `scaledToFill` | `.scaledToFill()` | `.with(ScaledToFill.of())` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C (Fill) |
660: | `minimumScaleFactor` | `.minimumScaleFactor(_:)` | `.with(MinimumScaleFactor.of(float))` | `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR` 0x001D |
661: 
662: **Semantics**: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` use the sentinels `FILL` (−1.0 = expand) and
663: `HUG_CONTENT` (−2.0 = intrinsic); omitting an axis leaves it to the native
664: renderer. SwiftUI's `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` / `maxHeight: .infinity` is
665: written by passing `Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (Java) / `f32::INFINITY` (Rust) to
666: the width/height overloads, which is normalized to `FILL` before emission. In
667: the min/ideal/max overload an infinite `maxWidth`/`maxHeight` means *no limit*
668: (the bound is omitted). `OFFSET` is a post-layout translation; `POSITION` is
669: absolute placement within the parent.

758: ### 5.6 Custom modifiers (developer-authored)
759: 
760: In SwiftUI any developer can define a modifier that applies to **any** existing
761: view — and Pathland is the same. This is a **first-class, MUST** property of
762: every conformant DSL: modifiers are never hard-bound to a view type.
763: 
764: - **Applicable to any view.** A modifier works on a library primitive
765:   (`Text`), a container (`VStack`), a control (`Button`), a custom view, or an
766:   already-modified view. The same modifier value applies everywhere.
767: - **One mechanism.** Core and application-authored modifiers are the **same
768:   surface**: a `ViewModifier` value applied via `.with(...)`. The library's
769:   sugar names (`.padding`, `.foregroundStyle`, …) are conveniences that
770:   construct the built-in `ViewModifier` values; there is exactly one modifier
771:   mechanism ([§5](#5-modifier-surface)). The Java realization ships **no sugar**
772:   — `.with(Padding.of(16))` is the only form (the varargs accept several at once).
773: 
774: | | Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) | Rust DSL (`pathland-view`) |
775: |-|-----------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|
776: | authoring | `struct Card: ViewModifier { func body(content: Content) -> some View }` | `@FunctionalInterface ViewModifier { View body(View content) }` | `trait ViewModifier { fn apply(&mut Node) }` |
777: | applying | `content.modifier(Card())` | `content.with(CardStyle.of(...))` / `content.with(A.of(...), B.of(...))` | `content.with(Card)` |
778: | sugar | `.padding(16)` ≡ `.modifier(Padding(16))` | **no sugar** — `.with(Padding.of(16))` only | `.padding(16.0)` ≡ `.with(Padding(16.0))` |
779: 
780: **Composition**: a custom modifier composes core modifiers **or** wraps
781: `content` with additional structure (a background, an overlay, a frame) and
782: returns the decorated view — exactly SwiftUI's `body(content: Content)`.
783: 
784: **Emission contract**: a custom modifier composed from core modifiers emits the
785: same one-`SET_PROPERTY`-per-property deltas as writing the modifiers inline;
786: emission stays diff-based, and a renderer that cannot apply a modifier
787: **allows and ignores** it.
788: 
789: **Realization deltas**:
790: - **Rust** — already conformant: every core modifier (`Padding`, `FontSize`,
791:   `ForegroundStyle`, `Frame`, …) implements `ViewModifier`, and the sugar
792:   methods delegate to `.with(...)`. Caveat: `apply(&mut Node)` mutates the
793:   built node's properties only — it cannot wrap `content` with new structure
794:   (the Java/SwiftUI `body(content)` form can). A conformant DSL's
795:   custom-modifier mechanism should support wrapping.
796: - **Java** — fully conformant: every core modifier is a `ViewModifier` value
797:   (`Padding.of(16)`, `ForegroundStyle.of(color)`, …) applied via `.with(...)`;
798:   `View` has no modifier sugar, and `buttonStyle` is the `ButtonStyleMod`
799:   modifier value (which binds the `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE` key down the
800:   subtree — subtree scoping is environment-only). Application-authored
801:   `ViewModifier.body(View)` is SwiftUI-shaped and can wrap content with structure.
802: 
803: ### 5.7 Styleable controls (the style contract)
804: 
805: A **style** customizes a view or control's *content*; the control owns its
806: *component and interaction*. This is one contract for every styleable surface
807: (`ButtonStyle`, `LabelStyle`, `AudioStyle`, `VideoStyle`, …), and it is the
808: author-facing shape of the protocol's **Composite Override Mode**
809: ([PRIMITIVES.md §2](./PRIMITIVES.md#2-dual-mode-rendering-pipeline--platform-delegation)).
810: 
811: - **The control owns the native component and the interaction.** A semantic
812:   control renders its **native control node** (its component id — `BUTTON`,
813:   `AUDIO`, …) and attaches its behavior to *that* node: the tap action /
814:   `EVENT_LISTENERS` (Button), the value/text/date sink, or the media sink
815:   (Audio/Video). The **whole control is interactive**, including its padding.
816: - **The style owns the content.** A style returns the control's **content view**
817:   from `makeBody(Configuration)`; the control attaches it as the control node's
818:   **single child**. The content keeps its own component(s), layout, and
819:   properties — a style **never** sets or overwrites the control's component and
820:   never wires the interaction. The result is a control with children → protocol
821:   **Composite Override Mode**.
822: - **Scoping is environment-only.** A style is scoped down a subtree with the
823:   matching `<Style>Mod` value, which binds the style's `EnvironmentKey` over the
824:   wrapped subtree (nearest wins); the control reads it via its
825:   `Environment.<name>Style()` accessor. This is the one inheritance mechanism
826:   ([§6 rule 6](#6-authoring-conventions)); `buttonStyle` binds
827:   `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE`, `audioStyle` `Environment.AUDIO_STYLE`,
828:   `videoStyle` `Environment.VIDEO_STYLE`, `labelStyle`
829:   `Environment.LABEL_STYLE`.
830: - **Defaults preserve the native path.** The default style contributes the
831:   control's natural content: `PlainButtonStyle` → the label;
832:   `NativeAudioStyle`/`NativeVideoStyle` → **no content** (an empty-content
833:   sentinel), so the control stays a **leaf** in Native Token Mode and the
834:   renderer shows native media controls; `DefaultLabelStyle` → title + icon.
835: - **Text/foreground modifiers cascade to content.** A `.foregroundStyle`/
836:   `.fontSize` (and the other inherited text modifiers) applied *to the control*
837:   reach the content's text — SwiftUI environment semantics. In the Java DSL the
838:   properties ride the control node; renderers cascade them to child text.
839: - **Main-axis alignment is the content's own layout — no protocol property.**
840:   A control's content box centers its child by default; to left-align a
841:   composite label (e.g. a navigation row), make the label full-width
842:   (`.frame(.infinity)`) and let its own `ALIGNMENT` place its content. There is
843:   deliberately no main-axis/justification property (the engine describes WHAT,
844:   never WHERE — [§1](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)).
845: - **Closed-variant ("token") styles are the same surface, not a wrapper.** Some
846:   styles select a whole native variant rather than supplying content:
847:   `ToggleStyle`/`PickerStyle`/`TextStyle` are wire **enums** applied as
848:   properties (`TOGGLE_STYLE`, …), and `LabelStyle` shapes which parts render.
849:   They are scoped/read exactly like the wrapper styles above.
850: 
851: Canonical signatures (SwiftUI-shaped) and the Java realization:
852: 
853: | Control | Style protocol | `Configuration` | Default style |
854: |---------|----------------|-----------------|---------------|
855: | `Button` | `ButtonStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | `(label: View)` | `PlainButtonStyle` (label) |
856: | `Label` | `LabelStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | `(title: View?, icon: View?)` | `DefaultLabelStyle` (title + icon) |
857: | `Audio` | `AudioStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | `(playing, position, volume, duration)` | `NativeAudioStyle` (no content) |
858: | `Video` | `VideoStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | `(playing, position, volume, duration)` | `NativeVideoStyle` (no content) |
859: 
860: ```java
861: // Button: the control wires the action; the style decorates the label.
862: enum MyButtonStyle implements ButtonStyle { INSTANCE;
863:     @Override public View makeBody(Configuration c) {
864:         return c.label().with(Padding.of(12), Background.of(BLUE));
865:     }
866: }
867: Button.of("Save", this::save).with(ButtonStyleMod.of(MyButtonStyle.INSTANCE));
868: 
869: // Label: the style decides which parts render (nullable parts = absent).
870: enum BadgeLabelStyle implements LabelStyle { INSTANCE;
871:     @Override public View makeBody(Configuration c) {
872:         return HStack.of(c.icon().with(FrameMod.of(18, 18)), c.title());
873:     }
874: }
875: ```
876: 
877: The Java DSL ships `PlainButtonStyle`/`BorderedButtonStyle`,
878: `DefaultLabelStyle`/`TitleOnlyLabelStyle`/`IconOnlyLabelStyle`, and
879: `NativeAudioStyle`/`NativeVideoStyle`; application-authored styles implement the
880: same interfaces. **Delta:** SwiftUI's `LabelStyleConfiguration.title`/`.icon`
881: are always-present views; Pathland passes `null` for an absent part (a style
882: checks `hasTitle()`/`hasIcon()`). And because the Java DSL has no per-modifier
883: sugar (§5), a style is applied with `.with(<Style>Mod.of(style))`.

887: ## 6. Authoring conventions
888: 
889: A conformant DSL follows these conventions:
890: 
891: 1. **Names**: SwiftUI view/modifier names; per-language case (camelCase,
892:    snake_case). `foregroundStyle` not `foregroundColor`; `fontWeight`,
893:    `multilineTextAlignment`, `scaledToFit`, `allowsHitTesting` keep their
894:    SwiftUI spellings.
895: 2. **Signature order**: canonical parameter order is preserved —
896:    `.border(color, width)`, `.frame(width, height, alignment)`,
897:    `.shadow(color, radius, x, y)`. Compound modifiers expand to one property
898:    per argument.
899: 3. **Constructor vs modifier**: structural (alignment, spacing) in the
900:    constructor; everything else chainable.
901: 4. **Typed enums**: `HorizontalAlignment` (leading/center/trailing, for
902:    `VStack`), `VerticalAlignment` (top/center/bottom, for `HStack`), `Alignment`
903:    (2D — topLeading … bottomTrailing — for `ZStack`/grids and the `frame`
904:    modifier's content alignment); all **position-only, never stretching** (a
905:    child's `FILL` size kind stretches). Plus `TextAlignment`, `FontWeight`
906:    (100–900), `Truncation` (head/middle/tail),
907:    `TextCase` (none/uppercase/lowercase), `FontStyle` (normal/italic),
908:    `FontDesign` (default/serif/rounded/monospaced), `ContentMode` (fit/fill),
909:    `ControlSize` (small/regular/large), `ToggleStyle`
910:    (switch/checkbox/button), `PickerStyle` (menu/segmented/wheel/radiogroup),
911:    `DatePickerMode` (date/time/dateAndTime), `ShapeKind`
912:    (circle/rectangle/roundedRectangle/capsule/ellipse/path). Numeric codes
913:    come from MODIFIERS.md's appendix; the DSL resolves them.
914: 5. **`Spacer`/`Color` as views**: `Spacer()` is a flexible expanding filler;
915:    `Color(...)` in a tree is a layout-greedy fill.
916: 6. **The environment is the only inheritance mechanism.** Any value that must
917:    reach a whole subtree — a style (`ButtonStyle`), the router, the active path,
918:    the session's persisted state — is injected through the environment, never
919:    threaded through constructors and never through a second scoping system. The
920:    environment is a hierarchical, nearest-wins scope of typed `EnvironmentKey`
921:    values (`View.environment(key, value)` / `Environment.value(key)`, Java;
922:    §4.5). A language MAY implement the scope with a thread-local over the
923:    synchronous render pass (Java does) — but that is the implementation of the
924:    one mechanism, not an additional one. A subtree-scoping modifier MUST be
925:    expressed as an `EnvironmentKey` binding: `buttonStyle` binds
926:    `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE` (`EnvironmentKey<ButtonStyle>`), exactly like the
927:    router and the active path.
928: 7. **Reactivity discipline**: `body()` is evaluated once; a signal read during
929:    mount records a dependency; a later write re-emits only the bound node.
930:    Never mutate signals during mount. The only structural re-evaluation is a
931:    structural container ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering)),
932:    which the emitter reconciles into `TREE` deltas.
933: 8. **Emission contract**: each DSL call emits exactly the documented
934:    properties with the documented value types; the emitter diffs. The DSL never
935:    computes layout, never positions, never serializes full trees.
936:

939: ## 7. Theme management
940: 
941: Pathland theming is **application-owned over a renderer-owned token system**
942: ([TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md); the wire encoding lives in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
943: §Design Token System). The DSL gives the author two distinct surfaces:
944: 
945: 1. **Token references in style modifiers** — semantic intent instead of a
946:    literal: `.foregroundStyle(Color.token("color.primary"))` emits a
947:    `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference the renderer resolves against the current scheme.
948:    No opcode is re-emitted when a token or the scheme changes.
949: 2. **Global theme overrides** — a batch of `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands
950:    rolled at mount: a single-scheme `Theme` or an `AdaptiveTheme` light+dark
951:    pair (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**).
952: 
953: > **Ownership**: the application owns theme values (base + `dark.*`) and token
954: > references; the renderer owns token defaults (light + dark), effective
955: > color-scheme detection, resolution (override → default → parent → fallback),
956: > and interaction-state styling (hover/pressed/focus/disabled). The protocol
957: > never transmits hover/click/transition styling.
958: 
959: ### 7.1 Token-typed values
960: 
961: Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY carry a
962: **token reference** instead of a literal value (MODIFIERS.md §Value types). The
963: reference rides the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) with the token path in
964: the arena — **never** a packed literal. A property carries exactly one value
965: (literal or reference, never both).
966: 
967: | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (current) | Rust DSL (current) | Emits |
968: |----------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|-------|
969: | `Color.token("color.primary")` | `Color.token("color.primary")` | `Color::token("color.primary")` | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref (`0x08`) in any COLOR-typed property: `COLOR` 0x100A (`.foregroundStyle`), `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001, `BORDER_COLOR` 0x1004, `SHADOW_COLOR` 0x1021, `TINT` 0x1030, … |
970: | `Color.token("dark.color.surface")` | `Color.token("dark.color.surface")` | `Color::token("dark.color.surface")` | same — an explicit dark-variant reference |
971: | `.padding(space.2)` / `Spacing(space.2)` | (token-valued spacing/padding) | (token-valued spacing/padding) | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref in a F32-typed property: `PADDING` 0x1011 / `SPACING` 0x0001 / `CONTENT_MARGINS` 0x0005, … (see TOKENS.md §Generative token families) |
972: 
973: `Color` keeps its dual identity: as a **View** it is a layout-greedy fill; as a
974: token reference (`Color.token(path)`) it is a **data value** passed to
975: style-taking modifiers. A token-typed property resolves renderer-side and
976: **re-resolves automatically** when the effective scheme changes — overrides and
977: scheme are renderer state, so no node is ever re-emitted for a theme/scheme
978: change.
979: 
980: Rules:
981: 
982: 1. Reference any token path — the standard catalog (TOKENS.md §Standard Token
983:    Catalog) or an application-defined path. A renderer that cannot apply a token
984:    falls back rather than erroring.
985: 2. `space.<N>` members are **generative**: reference them freely (`space.2`,
986:    `space.0.5`), but override only `space.base` (see §7.2 rule 2).
987: 3. A token reference must not be combined with a literal on the same property.
988: 
989: ### 7.2 Global theme overrides
990: 
991: A **theme** is a batch of token overrides. Every override defines **exactly one
992: value**; combine a light and a dark `Theme` via `AdaptiveTheme` for adaptive
993: theming.
994: 
995: | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) | Rust DSL (`pathland-view` / `pathland-engine`) | Emits |
996: |----------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|
997: | `Theme()` — one-scheme override batch | `new Theme()` (`ThemeData`) | `Theme::new()` | one `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` per override (`A` = arena path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value) |
998: | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `COLOR`-typed override (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`) |
999: | `.f32("space.base", 4.0)` | `.f32("space.base", 4.0f)` | `.f32("space.base", 4.0)` | `F32`-typed override (lengths in device pixels) |
1000: | `.u32("…", v)` / `.u8("…", v)` | `.u32(path, int)` / `.u8(path, int)` | `.u32(path, v)` / `.u8(path, v)` | `U32` / `U8`-typed override |
1001: | `.string("font.body.family", "Inter")` | `.string(path, String)` | `.string(path, "Inter")` | `STRING`-typed override (arena) |
1002: | `AdaptiveTheme(light, dark)` | `new AdaptiveTheme(light, dark)` | `AdaptiveTheme::new(light, dark)` | light overrides as base tokens; dark overrides `dark.`-prefixed |
1003: 
1004: Emission contract:
1005: 
1006: - The theme is emitted **once at mount** as a frame of
1007:   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcodes before the tree. Java: `new Emitter(sink,
1008:   theme)` emits it at the start of the mount and `renderFull` (resync) frames;
1009:   Rust: `Engine::apply_theme` / `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme`.
1010: - Overrides are **renderer state**: they never re-emit nodes and never
1011:   participate in the diff — an unchanged tree with a theme still emits **zero**
1012:   per-node opcodes.
1013: - `AdaptiveTheme` emits the light `Theme`'s overrides as base paths and the dark
1014:   `Theme`'s with the `dark.` prefix (added automatically when the author wrote a
1015:   bare path). The renderer derives the effective scheme from the platform and
1016:   resolves each override against it.
1017: - The renderer supplies light + dark defaults for the whole Tier 1 catalog, so
1018:   dark mode works even when the author only overrides base tokens.
1019: 
1020: Authoring rules:
1021: 
1022: 1. Override any token in the catalog or an application-defined path; never
1023:    assume specific renderer default values.
1024: 2. Override `space.base` to control the whole spacing scale — individual
1025:    `space.<N>` members MUST NOT be overridden.
1026: 3. Overrides are **global and renderer-wide**: apply the theme once per
1027:    session/host at mount, not per view.

1031: ## 8. Java DSL convergence (adopted)
1032: 
1033: The Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) has the complete surface. The convergence
1034: below has been **adopted** (`.of()` construction, the removal of the `View.*`
1035: factories, and modifiers as `ViewModifier` values); the remaining items are
1036: marked *optional*. The canonical contract is [§4](#4-view-surface) and
1037: [§5](#5-modifier-surface).
1038: 
1039: | Canonical | Java (adopted) | Optional / remaining |
1040: |-----------|----------------|----------------------|
1041: | `Text("…")` | `Text.of(String)` / `Text.of(Signal<String>)` | — |
1042: | `Button("…", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `Button.of(String, Runnable)` / `Button.of(View, Runnable)` | — |
1043: | `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `Toggle.of(String label, WritableSignal<Boolean>)` (+ `ToggleStyle` overload) | — |
1044: | `Slider(value: in:)` | `Slider.of(binding, min, max)` (binding first) | — |
1045: | `.border(color, width)` | `Border.of(Color, float)` via `.with(...)` | `Border.of(Color, float, float)` radius convenience |
1046: | `DatePicker(selection:)` | `DatePicker.of(mode, days)` | *optional* `Date`-shaped overload encoding days + millis-of-day per `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` |
1047: 
1048: Adopted conventions:
1049: 
1050: - **`.of()` is the one construction path.** Every concrete view/control exposes
1051:   a static `<ViewName>.of(...)` factory on its own class. Construction is never
1052:   `new <ViewName>()` and never `View.<name>(...)`.
1053: - **The `View.*` static-factory surface is removed.** The entire factory block
1054:   (`text`, `image`, `rectangle`, `spacer`, `vstack`, `hstack`, `zstack`,
1055:   `button`, `textField`, `textEditor`, `toggle`, `slider`, `stepper`,
1056:   `progressView`, `gauge`, `divider`, `grid`, `scrollView`, `lazyVStack`,
1057:   `lazyHStack`, `lazyVGrid`, `lazyHGrid`, `picker`, `menu`, `colorPicker`,
1058:   `datePicker`, `group`) is deleted from `View.java`.
1059: - **`Group` is a first-class view.** `Group.of(View...)` is a transparent
1060:   container view (SwiftUI `Group`).
1061: - **Core and custom modifiers share one mechanism.** Core modifiers are
1062:   `ViewModifier` values (`Padding.of(16)`, `ForegroundStyle.of(color)`) applied
1063:   via `.with(...)` — there is **no sugar on `View`**; several modifiers at
1064:   once use `.with(...)`, innermost-first. Parameterized modifier values use
1065:   `.of(...)`; `buttonStyle` is the `ButtonStyleMod` value (an environment
1066:   binding: it scopes `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE` down the subtree).
1067: - **Full `ShapeKind` coverage.** `Circle.of()`, `Capsule.of()`, `Ellipse.of()`,
1068:   `RoundedRectangle.of(cornerRadius:)`, generic `Shape.of(ShapeKind)` (for
1069:   `Path`).
1070: - *Optional*: an environment path letting the trailing-action form
1071:   (`Button(label) { action }`) read the action from the environment, if a
1072:   Java-idiomatic trailing lambda is desirable.
1073: - *Optional*: a `Date`-shaped `DatePicker` binding (see table).
1074: - Implementation status: `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`.
1075: 
1076: ---
1077: 
1078: ## 9. Generation contract for a new language
1079: 
1080: An AI (or a human) generating a Pathland DSL in a new language MUST produce the
1081: following and verify each item. This is a checklist; the authoritative details
1082: are the companion specs.
1083: 
1084: ### 9.1 Required surface
1085: 
1086: - [ ] **Views/controls** — every entry of [§4](#4-view-surface):
1087:   `Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape` (all `ShapeKind`s), `Divider`, `Spacer`,
1088:   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`; `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`,
1089:   `ScrollView`,
1090:   `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`; `Button`,
1091:   `TextField`, `SecureField`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
1092:   `Picker`, `Menu`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`.
1093: - [ ] **Modifiers** — every entry of [§5](#5-modifier-surface), chainable on
1094:   any view, innermost-first, emitting one property per underlying argument.
1095: - [ ] **Custom modifiers / unified mechanism** — a `ViewModifier` authoring
1096:   surface (`body(content) -> View`) + `.with(...)` chainable on **any**
1097:   view; **core modifiers are implemented through the same mechanism**, never a
1098:   separate syntax ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).
1099: - [ ] **Signals** — `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `untracked`,
1100:   `get`/`set`/`update`/`asReadonly`, with equality suppression, synchronous
1101:   flush, glitch-free propagation, error caching, write discipline, circular
1102:   detection ([§3.1](#31-signal-surface)).
1103: - [ ] **Two-way bindings** — every value control takes a writable signal and
1104:   exposes a sink the host routes its event into ([§3.2](#32-two-way-binding)).
1105: - [ ] **Persisted state** — `State<T>` keyed fields (or the language's
1106:   equivalent wiring) against a platform-neutral store ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)).
1107: - [ ] **Gestures** — `.onTapGesture` (composed from raw pointer down/up) and
1108:   raw `pointerEvents`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask ([§4.4](#44-gestures)).
1109: - [ ] **Structural reactivity (conditional rendering)** — a structural
1110:   container over a selector signal (`Conditional.when(...)` / `Case.of` /
1111:   `Case.otherwise`, or the language's `if`/`switch` equivalent), reconciling
1112:   the slot into `TREE` deltas with zero opcodes for identical structure
1113:   ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering)).
1114: - [ ] **Navigation** — `Router` / `RouteTable` / `NavigationContainer` /
1115:   `NavigationLink` over a plain `Signal<Route>`, the initial route host-seeded
1116:   before mount, emitting `ROUTE` and `TRANSITION` and consuming the `NAVIGATE`
1117:   event ([§4.5](#45-navigation)).
1118: - [ ] **Design tokens & theming** — a token surface: token-typed values usable
1119:   in style modifiers (a `Color` accepting a token path, e.g. `Color.token("color.primary")`
1120:   or the language's equivalent), a theme/override helper emitting
1121:   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base values + `dark.`-prefixed dark values), and
1122:   the **base=light / `dark.*`** color-scheme convention with renderer-derived
1123:   scheme detection — see [§7](#7-theme-management) and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md).
1124: 
1125: ### 9.2 Mapping rules (signature → protocol)
1126: 
1127: 1. Each view/control maps to its **fixed component id** in PRIMITIVES.md.
1128:    Application/custom component types live in `0x0100`–`0xFFFF`; a DSL must
1129:    never reuse allocated ids.
1130: 2. Each modifier maps to the **documented property id(s)** in MODIFIERS.md
1131:    with the documented **value type** (U8/U32/I32/F32/STRING/ENUM/COLOR/
1132:    DESIGN_TOKEN). Enumerated values use the numeric codes in MODIFIERS.md's
1133:    appendix.
1134: 3. `Color` values pack as sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`. A **token-typed** value instead
1135:    carries the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type with the token path in the arena
1136:    (never a packed literal); the renderer resolves it against the current
1137:    scheme. A theme/override helper emits `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
1138:    (`A` = arenaRef path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value); a `dark.`-prefixed path
1139:    supplies the dark design (base = light — [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).
1140: 4. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` sentinels: `FILL` = −1.0, `HUG_CONTENT` = −2.0.
1141: 5. `Grid` counts map to the **constructor properties** `GRID_COLUMNS` (`0x001E`) /
1142:    `GRID_ROWS` (`0x001F`): a positive `int` count emits a positive F32; absent =
1143:    auto-fit. A **`List<GridItem>`** overload serializes to the **`GRID_TRACKS`**
1144:    (`0x0020`, STRING) per-track spec, which takes precedence over the counts. A
1145:    `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` frame on a grid is the grid's **box**, never a count
1146:    ([§4.2](#42-layout--container-nodes)).
1147: 6. `DatePicker` value/event use the two-field encoding **days since epoch
1148:    (I32) + millis of day (U32)**; there is no `DATE_VALUE` property.
1149: 7. Value/text/date events are gated by the transport-aware event guards; the
1150:    DSL's controls emit the `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` that
1151:    declare intent.
1152: 8. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**: the DSL describes values, the
1153:    emitter diffs. A generated DSL must keep the retained tree + emitter
1154:    separation; it must not hand-serialize full trees.
1155: 
1156: ### 9.3 Language adaptation rules
1157: 
1158: | SwiftUI mechanism | Adapt as |
1159: |-------------------|----------|
1160: | trailing closure / result builder for children | varargs (Java), macros (Rust), builders/block (C#/Kotlin), element list (any) |
1161: | `Binding<T>` (Swift) | `WritableSignal<T>` (always — signals are the model, never property wrappers) |
1162: | `some View` opaque return | the language's `View` interface/trait (Java `View`, Rust `View` trait) |
1163: | `@State`/`@Binding` property wrappers | signals + persisted `State<T>` ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)) |
1164: | labeled parameters | named params where the language has them; otherwise preserve **parameter order** and document labels |
1165: | method chaining for modifiers | default methods (Java), extension traits (Rust), extension methods (C#/Kotlin) |
1166: 
1167: ### 9.4 Conformance recipe
1168: 
1169: A generated DSL is verified by proving it **emits the same bytes** as the
1170: reference implementations:
1171: 
1172: 1. Port the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) into the new
1173:    DSL's test harness; assert byte-identical `TREE`/`PARAMETER`/`EVENT`/`META`
1174:    opcodes for each canonical element.
1175: 2. Port the Java `EmitterTest` cases (mount → `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE`
1176:    deltas; unchanged tree → zero opcodes; two-way routing: `TEXT_CHANGED`,
1177:    `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED` write into the bound signal).
1178: 3. Verify the no-heap-allocation steady-state property where the target
1179:    language supports it (the Rust engine proves zero dynamic allocations during
1180:    steady-state emission).
1181: 4. Cross-check every referenced id against PRIMITIVES.md/MODIFIERS.md/EVENTS.md
1182:    (the specs are the source of truth, never the reference code).
1183: 
1184: **Reference implementations to read**: Java — `lib/java/pathland-view`
1185: (`com.pathland.view`, `com.pathland.view.signal`, `com.pathland.view.state`,
1186: `com.pathland.view.emit`); Rust — `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view` +
1187: `pathland-engine` + `pathland-core::signal`.
1188: 
1189: ---
1190: 
1191: ## 10. Appendix A: SwiftUI ↔ DSL signature map

1194: [§5](#5-modifier-surface).
1195:

162: /// A composable view. Implement for custom views; the core components and
163: /// `Modified` wrappers implement it already.
164: pub trait View {
165:     /// Build the retained node for this view.
166:     fn build(&self) -> Node;
167: }
168: 
169: /// A view decorator (SwiftUI `ViewModifier`): transforms a node's properties.
170: ///
171: /// Core modifiers (`Spacing`, `Padding`, `FontSize`, `Color`, `Background`)
172: /// implement this; application code implements it to compose custom modifiers.
173: pub trait ViewModifier {
174:     /// Apply the modifier to `node` (mutating constraint properties).
175:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node);
176: }
177: 
178: /// A view wrapped by a modifier (SwiftUI `some View` nesting).
179: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
180: pub struct Modified<V, M> {
181:     view: V,
182:     modifier: M,
183: }
184: 
185: impl<V: View, M: ViewModifier> View for Modified<V, M> {
186:     fn build(&self) -> Node {
187:         let mut node = self.view.build();
188:         self.modifier.apply(&mut node);
189:         node
190:     }
191: }
192: 
193: /// Blanket modifier methods on any `View`.
194: ///
195: /// `.with(...)` applies a custom (or core) modifier; the sugar methods
196: /// (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`, `background`) are conveniences
197: /// that construct the corresponding core modifier. Modifiers apply
198: /// innermost-first, matching SwiftUI ordering.
199: pub trait ViewExt: View + Sized {
200:     /// Apply a modifier to this view.
201:     fn with<M: ViewModifier>(self, modifier: M) -> Modified<Self, M> {
202:         Modified { view: self, modifier }
203:     }
204: 
205:     /// Chain `.spacing(value)`.
206:     fn spacing(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, Spacing> {
207:         self.with(Spacing(value))
208:     }
209: 
210:     /// Chain `.padding(value)`.
211:     fn padding(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, Padding> {
212:         self.with(Padding(value))
213:     }
214: 
215:     /// Chain `.font_size(value)`.

223:     /// `font_size`/`font_weight`/`font_family`/`font_design` layer on top.
